newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KNP BT uses sell-off proceeds to restructure.
newsitem.headline: KNP BT uses sell-off proceeds to restructure.

text.p: Dutch paper group KNP BT said on Thursday it had set aside the lion's share of a 200 million guilder extraordinary gain from divestments for restructuring at its paper and packaging units.
It said the extraordinary gain, generated mainly from the sale of its plastic packaging activities, was offset by extraordinary charges of 175 million.
"These (charges) are related to provisions in connection with reorganisations currently under way within KNP Leykam and KNP BT Packaging," it said in a statement.
Pre-tax extraordinaries amounted to a 25 million guilder gain or 20 million guilders net of tax, it said.
The restructuring measures would aim to improve capacity utilisation of existing plant and the previously announced phased job losses stretching to 1999, it said.
"These measures will lead to further improvement in the profitability of the paper production and packaging activities," KNP BT said.
